description: Search and retrieve workspace messages and transcriptions using simple keyword search, AI-powered semantic search, and flexible filtering

tools.name: workspace_simple_search
tools.description: Fast full-text keyword search across workspace messages and transcriptions. Uses PostgreSQL ILIKE for simple pattern matching. Fast, reliable, and doesn't require OpenAI API. Use this when you need quick keyword-based search or when semantic search is not available.

search_query.description: Text to search for. Supports % wildcards for partial matching. Case-insensitive.

workspace_ids.description: List of workspace IDs to search. If omitted, searches all workspaces the user has access to.

user_id.description: Filter results to specific user ID. If omitted, searches messages/transcriptions from all users.

search_messages.description: Include workspace messages in search results. Set to false to search only transcriptions.

search_transcriptions.description: Include transcriptions in search results. Set to false to search only messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return across both messages and transcriptions. Higher limits may cause token overflow.

messages.description: Array of matching messages with full details

transcriptions.description: Array of matching transcriptions with full details

total_count.description: Total number of results returned (messages + transcriptions)

query.description: The search query that was executed

examples.name: Search for database discussions in specific workspaces
examples.description: Find all messages and transcriptions mentioning 'database performance' in workspaces 1, 2, and 3

examples.name: Search only transcriptions for keyword
examples.description: Search only transcriptions (not messages) for 'quarterly report'

examples.name: Find what a specific user said
examples.description: Find all messages/transcriptions from user 5 mentioning 'pricing' in workspace 1

examples.name: Wildcard search for variations
examples.description: Find messages containing both 'deploy' and 'production' in any order

notes: ✅ FAST: Uses PostgreSQL ILIKE - very quick even on large datasets
✅ RELIABLE: No dependencies on external APIs
✅ SIMPLE: Just matches keywords - no AI understanding
❌ LIMITED: Won't find 'SQL optimization' when searching for 'database performance'
💡 TIP: Use wildcards (%) for flexible matching: '%performance%issue%'
💡 TIP: Case-insensitive by default (ILIKE operator)
⚠️ LIMIT: Returns chronological results, not relevance-ranked

tools.name: workspace_semantic_search
tools.description: AI-powered semantic search using OpenAI embeddings and vector similarity. Understands meaning and context, not just exact keywords. Searching for 'database performance' will find results about 'SQL optimization', 'query speed', and 'data store performance' even without exact keyword matches. Requires pgvector extension and populated embeddings.

search_query.description: Natural language description of what you're looking for. The AI will understand the meaning and find semantically similar content.
examples: Tell me about pricing strategy discussions
What did Sarah say about the Q4 goals?
meetings where we discussed hiring plans

workspace_ids.description: List of workspace IDs to search. If omitted, searches all workspaces.

user_id.description: Filter results to specific user ID. If omitted, searches all users.

similarity_threshold.description: Minimum similarity score (0.0-1.0) for results. Higher values = more strict matching. 0.7 is recommended for general use, 0.8+ for very precise matches.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return. Results are ranked by similarity score (most relevant first).

results.description: Array of messages ranked by similarity score (most relevant first)

query.description: The search query that was executed

similarity_threshold.description: The threshold used for filtering results

examples.name: Find pricing discussions without exact keywords

input.search_query: Tell me about pricing strategy discussions

examples.description: Will find messages about 'cost structure', 'revenue model', 'pricing tiers' even if they don't mention 'pricing strategy' exactly

examples.name: Search for database performance topics
examples.description: Will find messages about 'SQL optimization', 'query speed', 'data store performance', 'slow queries' even without exact keyword matches

examples.name: Find what a user said about a topic

input.search_query: What did Sarah say about Q4 goals?

examples.description: Semantic search for user 5's messages about quarterly objectives, targets, milestones, etc.

examples.name: High-precision search for specific topic
examples.description: Very strict matching (0.85 threshold) for highly relevant results only

requirements: ✅ pgvector extension must be enabled on PostgreSQL
✅ embedding_vector column must be type vector(1536), not TEXT
✅ Embeddings must be populated for existing messages
✅ OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable must be set
✅ OpenAI Python library must be installed (pip install openai)
notes: 🤖 AI-POWERED: Uses OpenAI text-embedding-3-small model
🎯 SEMANTIC: Understands meaning, not just keywords
📊 RANKED: Results sorted by similarity score (most relevant first)
💰 COST: ~$0.02 per 1M tokens (~500,000 searches)
⚡ SPEED: Slightly slower than simple search (~200-500ms)
💡 TIP: Use natural language queries like 'What did we discuss about...'
💡 TIP: Lower threshold (0.6-0.7) for broader results, higher (0.8+) for precision
⚠️ FALLBACK: If semantic search fails, automatically suggests workspace_simple_search
⚠️ SETUP: Requires one-time migration to enable pgvector and populate embeddings

error_vector_extension.message: pgvector extension not enabled or embedding_vector column not configured
error_vector_extension.solution: Run the migration script: python tools/migrations/enable_pgvector.py

error_no_results.message: No results found above similarity threshold
error_no_results.alternative: Use workspace_simple_search to verify data exists

tools.name: workspace_get_messages
tools.description: Retrieve workspace messages with flexible filtering by thread, session, user, role, date range, or any combination. Use this to get conversation context, thread history, or specific message sets. Supports pagination for large result sets.

workspace_ids.description: List of workspace IDs to retrieve messages from. If omitted, retrieves from all workspaces.

thread_id.description: Retrieve all messages from a specific thread. Useful for getting complete conversation context.

session_id.description: Retrieve all messages from a specific session.

user_id.description: Filter to messages from a specific user.

role.description: Filter by message role. 'user' = user messages, 'assistant' = AI responses, 'system' = system messages.

date_from.description: Start date for date range filter (inclusive). Only messages on or after this date.

date_to.description: End date for date range filter (inclusive). Only messages on or before this date.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Use with offset for pagination.

offset.description: Number of messages to skip (for pagination). offset=100 with limit=50 returns messages 101-150.

messages.description: Array of message objects with full details (id, content, role, timestamps, user info, workspace info)

total_count.description: Total number of messages matching filters (not just returned count)

returned_count.description: Number of messages in this response

filters_applied.description: Summary of filters that were applied

has_more.description: True if there are more results beyond this page

examples.name: Get recent messages from workspace
examples.description: Retrieve the 50 most recent messages from workspace 1

examples.name: Get entire thread conversation
examples.description: Retrieve all messages from thread 42 to see complete conversation context

examples.name: Get user messages in date range
examples.description: Get all messages from user 5 during the first week of December

examples.name: Get all AI responses in workspace
examples.description: Retrieve all AI assistant responses from workspace 1

examples.name: Paginate through large result set
examples.description: Get messages 101-200 (second page) from workspaces 1 and 2

examples.name: Get session messages for specific user
examples.description: Get all messages from user 5 in session 789

notes: 📊 PAGINATION: Use limit + offset to page through large result sets
🕒 ORDER: Results ordered by created_at DESC (newest first)
🔍 FLEXIBLE: Combine any filters - all are optional
💡 TIP: Use thread_id to get complete conversation context
💡 TIP: Use role='assistant' to see only AI responses
💡 TIP: Check has_more=true to know if there are more results
⚠️ LIMIT: Max 500 messages per request to prevent token overflow
⚠️ PERFORMANCE: Filtering by thread_id or session_id is faster than date ranges

tools.name: workspace_get_transcriptions
tools.description: Retrieve transcriptions with flexible filtering by workspace, session, user, transcription mode, duration, date range, or any combination. Automatically excludes deleted transcriptions. Supports pagination for large result sets.

workspace_ids.description: List of workspace IDs to retrieve transcriptions from. If omitted, retrieves from all workspaces.

session_id.description: Retrieve all transcriptions from a specific session.

user_id.description: Filter to transcriptions from a specific user.

transcription_mode.description: Filter by transcription mode. 'web_speech' = browser API, 'whisper' = OpenAI Whisper, 'hybrid' = both.

date_from.description: Start date for date range filter (inclusive).

date_to.description: End date for date range filter (inclusive).

min_duration.description: Minimum transcription duration in seconds. Use to filter for longer recordings.

max_duration.description: Maximum transcription duration in seconds. Use to filter for shorter recordings.

limit.description: Maximum number of transcriptions to return. Use with offset for pagination.

offset.description: Number of transcriptions to skip (for pagination).

transcriptions.description: Array of transcription objects with full details (id, text, whisper_text, mode, duration, timestamps, user info, workspace info)

total_count.description: Total number of transcriptions matching filters

returned_count.description: Number of transcriptions in this response

filters_applied.description: Summary of filters that were applied

has_more.description: True if there are more results beyond this page

examples.name: Get recent transcriptions from workspace
examples.description: Retrieve the 20 most recent transcriptions from workspace 1

examples.name: Get all transcriptions from session
examples.description: Retrieve all transcriptions from session 789

examples.name: Get long transcriptions (over 2 minutes)
examples.description: Find transcriptions longer than 2 minutes (120 seconds)

examples.name: Get Whisper AI transcriptions from date range
examples.description: Get all Whisper AI transcriptions from the first week of December

examples.name: Get short transcriptions for testing
examples.description: Find transcriptions 30 seconds or shorter

examples.name: Get user's hybrid transcriptions
examples.description: Get all hybrid-mode transcriptions from user 5 in workspaces 1 and 2

notes: 🗑️ AUTO-FILTER: Automatically excludes deleted transcriptions (deleted_at IS NULL)
📊 PAGINATION: Use limit + offset to page through large result sets
🕒 ORDER: Results ordered by created_at DESC (newest first)
🔍 FLEXIBLE: Combine any filters - all are optional
📝 TEXT: Both 'text' (Web Speech) and 'whisper_text' (Whisper AI) are returned
💡 TIP: Use min_duration to find substantial recordings
💡 TIP: Use transcription_mode='whisper' for highest quality transcriptions
💡 TIP: Check has_more=true to know if there are more results
⚠️ LIMIT: Max 200 transcriptions per request to prevent token overflow

workspace_simple_search: User asks to 'search for' or 'find' with specific keywords
Need fast results without AI processing
Semantic search is not available or configured
Searching for exact phrases or specific words
workspace_semantic_search: User asks 'What did we discuss about...' or 'Tell me about...'
Need to understand meaning, not just keywords
User describes a concept without exact keywords
Example: 'What pricing strategies did we discuss?' (finds 'cost model', 'revenue approach', etc.)
workspace_get_messages: User wants to see conversation history
Need messages from specific thread or session
Filtering by user, role, or date range
Getting AI responses or user messages separately
Example: 'Show me all messages from thread 42' or 'Get user messages from last week'
workspace_get_transcriptions: User wants to see transcription history
Filtering by duration, mode, or date range
Example: 'Show me all Whisper transcriptions over 2 minutes'

workflow_1_context_retrieval.name: Get conversation context for current thread
steps: 1. Use workspace_get_messages with thread_id to get all messages
2. Review message history to understand context
3. Use that context to provide informed responses

workflow_2_topic_search.name: Find all discussions about a topic
steps: 2. If semantic search fails, fall back to workspace_simple_search
3. Review results and provide summary to user

workflow_3_user_activity.name: Get all activity from specific user

workflow_4_session_review.name: Review everything from a session
steps: 3. Present chronological summary of session activity

performance_tips: ✅ Use workspace_ids filter to reduce search scope
✅ Use date ranges for recent data (last 7 days, last month)
✅ Start with lower limits (20-50) to avoid token overflow
✅ Use thread_id or session_id filters for fastest queries
✅ Semantic search is slower but more accurate - use wisely
⚠️ Large result sets (200+) may cause token overflow
⚠️ Avoid very broad date ranges without other filters
⚠️ Semantic search requires OpenAI API call (~200-500ms delay)
error_handling: If semantic search fails → Automatically suggests simple search fallback
If no results found → Try lowering similarity_threshold or using wildcards
If token overflow → Reduce limit or add more filters
If connection fails → Check database credentials and network

for_simple_search: ✅ No additional setup needed - works out of the box
for_semantic_search: ✅ embedding_vector column converted to vector(1536) type
✅ OpenAI Python library installed (pip install openai)
